item.title: Yamagata Cherries: Japan's Cherry Capital — Guide
item.description: Yamagata produces approximately 70% of Japan’s entire cherry harvest, and the prefecture takes enormous pride in its sato nishiki and beni-shuho varieties — large, deeply coloured, intensely sweet cherries that retail as premium gifts. The Higashine and Sagae areas are the cherry heartland, with all-you-can-eat pick-your-own orchards from mid-June through July, and nearby wineries offering cellar tours amid the same mountain-valley scenery. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Higashine & Sagae, Yamagata Hours Orchards ~mid-Jun–Jul Admission Picking ~¥1,500–2,000 (30 min) Time needed 1–2 hours Best time Mid-June–July (cherry season) What to Try All-you-can-eat picking of sato nishiki and beni-shuho.
